lines.say: Why do you lift more when you shout?
Why does this happen, number fifteen.
In a famous study from nineteen sixty-one, people shouted just before pulling, and their strength went up.
Later studies found it too. A short, loud shout made people squeeze harder, and tennis players who grunted hit the ball faster.
Scientists think the shout helps your brain fire more muscle at once, and braces your core.
It also gives you a quick rush, like a burst of adrenaline.
But don't hold your breath for the whole set, and don't scare everyone in the gym.
A short grunt on your hardest reps is enough.
